description: v1.25.0 (EP-30-W1b, THE DECLARED STREAM KEY'S FIRST USE: op:UNBIND's declaration names the stream its records are written under; a MINOR because ONE shipped operation's declaration gains a key the engine already honours, no check kind is added and none removed, no operation is added or removed, and every other declaration is byte-unchanged): THE DOOR AN ACT ENTERS DECIDED THE STREAM ITS DECLARATION LANDED IN, and which stream a law writes into is LAW CONTENT rather than a property of the door — the conflation EP-30-W1a removed from the engine and that this pass is the first law to use. op:UNBIND now declares `record_stream: BIND-DEVICE`, so AN UNBIND RECORD LANDS IN THE GRANTING ACT'S STREAM WHILE STILL RECORDING THAT UNBIND WROTE IT: `action` is untouched and goes on carrying the door where every existing reader already looks, `record_stream` names only where the declaration lands, and a record shape that could not carry BOTH facts would have been a STOP AND RAISE rather than an overwrite — an amending record that hid its own author would be a record holding an act nobody performed. WHAT IT BUYS: `prior_value`'s latest-seq-wins now MEETS the revoking act. EP-30-E1 established that the thirteenth kind ALREADY expresses revocation, on condition that the revoking record is reachable from the granting act's stream — it separated ADMIT/REFUSE where grant and revoke were one operation and gave ADMIT/ADMIT against this estate's SEPARATE op:UNBIND, and that blindness is exactly what this pass removes. NOTHING NEW IS REFUSED AND THAT IS THE DESIGN: no consuming operation gains a check here, so every act admitted before this pass is admitted after it; making revocation BITE is EP-30-W2, and the fact becomes VISIBLE here before it becomes BINDING there. THE DECLARED-LAW CENSUS DOES NOT MOVE: 76 ops and 43 laws unchanged, ONE declaration amended, no record removed.

an answer from outside the S-plane binds to its hand-out by the STORE's own citation: a crossing record naming no hand-out, or naming one already answered or superseded by a re-judge, is refused. What a record claims about itself in its own content carries no binding — only the store's record of the hand-out does, because nothing binds a token to a hand-out except the store's record of it.

an external answer is accepted only against the world it was judged in: the hand-out records the canonical hash of its declared input-view, the return recomputes that view under the same pinned version, and an answer whose seal moved — or whose acceptance ran no seal check at all — is refused. Staleness is not an authority verdict and never substitutes for one: a chain revoked mid-crossing refuses on authority with the seal holding, and a moved read-set refuses on staleness with every act still lawful. The two verdicts carry different information and are never merged.

what happens when an answer returns stale, unless the station names its own policy under `crossing-stale-policy:<STATION>`: `re-judge` mints a fresh crossing at the current head, parent-linked to the stale one, and `abort` leaves the stale refusal standing. Never a silent execute; never a silent drop — the refusal is recorded citing the staleness rule either way, and a case the machine may not retry surfaces on the re-ask view for a human.

how many re-judges one crossing chain may spend before the stale refusal stands and the case surfaces for a human re-ask, unless the station names its own budget under `crossing-retry-budget:<STATION>`. A retry budget is recorded policy with a named owner (the root, until a grant says otherwise), never a constant in code; what a chain has already spent is counted from the parent links in the record, so there is no attempt counter to rot.

a SHARE of a region moves from one entity to others by a recorded, rule-citing decision that NAMES THE REGION IT IS OVER, and the region is one A PRIOR RECORD FOUNDED rather than a string the caller supplies. THE GRANT INHERITS THE REGION'S ESTABLISHMENT AND NEVER MINTS IT: `MEM-GRANT` is the region's establishing act (`object_param: region`, its payload carrying `region` and `holder`), so a share over a region no MEM-GRANT founds is a grant of nothing, appended as though it were a grant of something — it is REFUSED, citing this rule. One identity derived twice is two answers waiting to disagree, and the disagreement would be invisible because both sides would be internally consistent. WHO SHARES WHAT NOW IS DERIVED, never stored: it is a fold of these decisions, so killing every derived structure and replaying the record alone returns the same answer. The granter is an ATTRIBUTION STAMPED TO THE ACTING ACTOR and is never read from the caller's supplied value. SEEDED with the operation that cites it, because no refusal path may cite a rule name the founding does not contain (the EP-25 ADDENDUM 4 containment line) — this operation has cited this rule since it shipped and the pack has never held it, so until now its every refusal would have named nothing. WHAT THIS RULE DOES NOT YET REACH, STATED IN THE LAW ITSELF SO NO READER INFERS COVER IT DOES NOT HAVE: it does not ask WHETHER THE PARTIES BEING GRANTED ACCESS ARE ESTABLISHED ENTITIES, and it does not ask WHETHER THE GRANTER HOLDS THE REGION. Neither omission is a choice. `grantees` is MANY-VALUED and the check vocabulary HAS NO QUANTIFIER, so a many-valued parameter cannot be asked anything at all — not every, not any, not none; the capability rides EP-30-K2 and the wiring rides EP-30-C4W. The granter question needs a record bound by one parameter and a field of it compared against another, which is EP-30-K1's `bound_field`, and wiring it onto this operation rides EP-30-C4W. A LAW THAT CLAIMED THE COVER IT DOES NOT HAVE WOULD BE WORSE THAN THE DANGLING CITATION IT REPLACES.

custody of an OPEN HANDLE moves between ENTITIES by a recorded, rule-citing decision that NAMES BOTH PARTIES (design/10 §8: fd passing is itself a recorded custody transfer, and the pidfd_getfd row calls moving a custody grant across processes a DECISION; design/39 §4: handing another program an open file is a custody transfer THROUGH the border, recorded). The file is not a party to it, so an attribute on the file cannot carry it: an attribute value is any string a caller writes, while a party is a recorded establishment, and a transfer whose giver or receiver is a bare value names nobody — it is REFUSED, citing this rule. That refusal is what makes the entity vocabulary established rather than merely declared. THE DEVICE THE HANDLE STANDS ON IS INHERITED AND NEVER RE-DERIVED: the transfer names a device a prior binding founded under DEV-LAW-BIND, and the channel side computes no identity of its own — one identity derived twice is two answers waiting to disagree, and the disagreement would be invisible because both sides would be internally consistent. A stored holder field is a frozen copy of the record and rots away from it silently, which is the one failure a derived answer cannot have. payload.text: every judged or authorised act has two times, and they carry different halves. The DECIDING time is the moment the thing became authorised in the decider's hands, and that is where legitimacy is created. The RECORDING time is the moment the store wrote it, and that is where order is created; record_time remains the sole total-order anchor and nothing in this rule moves it. A decision binds from its deciding moment, not from its arrival: arrival order never adjudicates. The store's acceptance test is a legitimacy-transfer test — an arriving decision is evaluated against the law in force AS OF ITS DECIDING TIME, with its seal as proof of the world it was decided in, while its actor's AUTHORITY is evaluated LIVE at effect time. A chain revoked between the deciding moment and the arrival refuses at the door however sound the deciding time was, and that refusal carries authority information rather than staleness information; the two verdicts are never merged. A law-family record whose deciding time EQUALS an act's deciding time is not in force for that act — the comparison is strict, at the ordinary door and in the reconciliation sweep alike, because one rule applied twice cannot resolve the same pair of facts two ways.

when law arrives whose deciding time precedes already-recorded acts, the store rewrites nothing. It computes which recorded acts the law reaches — acts decided strictly after the law's own deciding moment and recorded before the law arrived, whose admission the law flips — and appends OVERTURN decisions, each citing the reaching law (or, where the reach was transitive, the overturned ancestor whose exclusion reached it), the overturned act, and both deciding times. Views answer with the reconciled state from the overturn's own recording time forward; an asOf answer from before the overturn still shows the act's effect, because order is untouched and validity is what changed. Overturning is ordinary governed activity: recorded, rule-citing, attributable, replayable, and subject to every standing check including the protected-core floor and the conservation law. A REFUSAL is never converted into a done act: a late-arriving permissive law appends nothing, because an overturn cannot perform an act that never happened and a record claiming an effect that did not occur is the one forbidden lie — the case surfaces for re-asking and the actor re-submits at the current head. An act once overturned is never un-overturned. A sweep computes its rounds to a fixed point before it appends anything, and appends nothing at all if the post-state it computed would leave any chain without a root or move root; that sweep routes to the owner instead. A law-family arrival that would reach recorded acts is not accepted while a sweep is running — the running sweep settles the record first, so two identical inputs cannot give two results by interleaving.

a claimed deciding time cannot predate the store-state its own seal pins. Deciding timestamps are caller-asserted until they are cryptographically signed, and that cap is stated rather than hidden; what the seal closes is one direction of it. The seal is the recorded hash of exactly what the decider was shown, so the world it pins has a first moment, and a decision cannot be claimed at 9:00 over a world that only came into being at 9:10. An arrival whose claimed deciding time no store state at or before it could have produced is refused, cited. The other direction — a claimed time running later than the true one — stays open until record signing closes it.

a decider's live working context is recorded: a session-open naming the account and its read-set, and a session-close ending it. The registry is a derived view over those two records and holds nothing. The read-set is DECLARED rather than derived, and that is necessity rather than laziness — reads append nothing by design, so the store cannot compute what a session has looked at. Under-declaration costs a session deliveries it would have wanted; it never costs legitimacy, because the seal still faces every decision at acceptance. A read-set is declared as view references and resolved at use, never stored resolved, because a resolved copy is a frozen derivative of a definition that can be amended underneath it.

LANE PRIORITY AND THE LANE BUDGET — law travels faster than traffic (design/35 §3, owner-ruled 2026-07-25; design/36 K10). Law-family records are processed and delivered ahead of ordinary records in BOTH directions, and lane membership is a property of the record's own class read from the record — a record rides the law lane because its payload declares a rule_id, never because a list somewhere names its verb. An overturn rides ORDINARY: it is a DECISION, and the sweep rather than the lane is its urgency. The store's total order is untouched by any of this: the lane changes the SCHEDULING of processing, never record_time's authority (design/21, design/35 §5). PROPOSED DEFAULT, awaiting the owner's values (wall primitive 8, priced with design/23's levers). `cycle` is the number of deliveries one drain cycle may serve, and a cycle is ONE APPEND — never a tick and never a second, so the whole schedule is a function of the record's own order (the 15.1 clock ban). `reserve` is the slice of every cycle that ONLY the lane named first in `order` may spend; it is what lets a law delivery leave from behind an ordinary backlog of any depth, and with it set to zero the law lane competes in arrival order and starves under a standing flood. `depth` caps how many deliveries may wait on a lane; over the cap the oldest waiting delivery on that lane is SHED, citing this rule. A shed drops a DERIVED FLOW and never a fact — the act stays on the record permanently, and both the shed and its reason are computed rather than appended, because under a flood the sheds are exactly proportional to the flood and appending one record each would make recording scale with operation (I9). No law lane is ever shed; the reserve exists so it never has to be. FAIL-OPEN ON DELIVERY: with this policy absent from the record nothing is capped and nothing is shed, which is the pre-EP-27 behaviour exactly — there is no code-resident default standing in for a missing law.

THE DEVICE BINDING LAW. Binding a device to a driver is a recorded DECISION that cites a registered driver capability, and unbinding is a recorded decision that cites a prior bind. SEEDED as a record here at EP-29 W1a so that no device definition and no device refusal path cites a rule name the founding does not contain: BIND-DEVICE and UNBIND have cited this id since campaign 1 while no record declared it. WHAT A BIND GRANTS, STATED SO NOTHING HAS TO INFER IT: a bind grants CUSTODY of the device and NOT I/O. Custody is the right to be the bound driver; it is not admission to move bytes. I/O ADMISSION CITES A WINDOW DECLARATION BY NAME, and a window is declared under this law. AND THE WINDOW-ABSENT CASE IS DECLARED HERE RATHER THAN DEFAULTED: where this law declares no window for an act, the act is PERMITTED BY NOTHING, so the gate REFUSES it and RECORDS the refusal citing the tip-level terminal rule that an act class no declaration founds does not exist. That sentence is written rather than left to an engine default on purpose — a default filling a declaration gap with permission would be a second source of truth about what this world's law declares, and this law admits none. A REGISTRATION THAT ENUMERATES NO CAPABILITIES ENUMERATES NOTHING, and containment over it therefore permits nothing; a capability is what it names, never what it omits. THE WINDOW DECLARATIONS HAVE LANDED (EP-29 W1b, founding 1.20.0). They were held back until their surfaces were established at the guest, because a window declared before its surfaces are established is law authored against a world nobody has read. The surfaces were established by driving at the guest on 2026-08-12: three notification surfaces, of which device@sysfs and device@uevent see device APPEARANCE and BINDS and DISCLAIM device I/O in their own coverage, and arrival@tracepoints — the one whose class IS I/O arrivals — carries the subject and is readable ONLY BY A PRIVILEGED OBSERVER. So the windows declared under this law cite arrival@tracepoints and NAME THAT PRIVILEGE AS A COST rather than hiding it, and they do not borrow a reachable surface for a subject it disclaims. WHAT IS PERMITTED IS NOW EXACTLY WHAT THE DECLARED WINDOWS NAME AND NOTHING ELSE: an act class this law founds no declaration for is still permitted by nothing and still refuses, recorded, citing the tip-level terminal rule. The refusal was NARROWED, never removed.
payload.enforced_by: the require_prior checks on BIND-DEVICE (a bind cites a registered capability) and on UNBIND (an unbind cites a prior bind), and the gate's closure step, which refuses and records any act class this law founds no declaration for

payload.text:
THE DEVICE INTAKE LAW — AT WHAT GRANULARITY AN ADMITTED DEVICE INPUT ARRIVAL IS RECORDED. DEV-LAW-BIND governs ADMISSION: a bind grants custody and not I/O, and I/O admission cites a window declaration by name. THIS law governs the RECORD: how many admitted arrivals one recorded INPUT covers. It is DECLARED, never defaulted, and a declaration under it is made by DECLARE-INTAKE citing this law. 

THE NEVER-CLAUSE, WHICH IS THIS LAW'S POINT AND IS LAW TEXT RATHER THAN COMMENTARY: AN ADMITTED INPUT ARRIVAL IS NEVER RECORDED AT PER-INTERRUPT GRADE. Interrupts arrive at device rate and the record does not. A recorded INPUT covers a WINDOW of arrivals and cites the intake declaration that bounds that window. NO DECLARATION UNDER THIS LAW MAY SET A BOUND OF ONE, at any load and for any device class: a covering record standing for exactly one arrival is the per-interrupt grade wearing a window's name. 

WHAT A COVERING RECORD CARRIES, so the never-clause costs no visibility and CONST-RECORDING-TOTAL's floor is met rather than argued around: the COUNT of arrivals covered, the BYTE TOTAL over them, the device the arrivals were attributed to, the window they were admitted under by name, and this law's citation together with the intake declaration's name. NEVER THE CONTENT — device I/O content is STREAM and is classified out, which the window declarations already state in their own does_not_see. A covering record makes no governed act invisible: it names how many there were and how many bytes they moved. 

THE GRANULARITY VALUES ARE MEASURED AND NOT ASSERTED. Every numeric value in a declaration under this law names the calibration cell it derives from, that cell's POPULATION and its BASIS, and the DERIVATION that picks the number rather than a neighbouring one (charter §A51). THREE CONSTRAINTS ON THE DERIVATION, each established by measurement at EP-29 W2a on 2026-08-13 and each written here because a later author will otherwise re-take the wrong column: 
(1) A VALUE DERIVES FROM THE ARRIVAL COUNT, NEVER FROM AN ARRIVAL RATE. Identical commands repeated three times gave arrival COUNTS at max/min ratio 1.0000 on every block cell and RATES at ratio up to 1.6265 — a rate's denominator is the window's own elapsed time, and at these window sizes that measures scheduling. 
(2) A VALUE STANDS ON DELIVERED LOAD, NEVER ON REQUESTED LOAD. A command's own number is not a population: `dd count=256` against a 366 KiB device delivered 92. Where a load tool reports no delivery figure, NO per-act value may be derived at all, and the declaration states the value UNESTABLISHED with its reason rather than dividing by the request. 
(3) A VALUE IS DECLARED PER DEVICE CLASS. Block held exactly 1.0 interrupts and exactly 3.0 arrivals per delivered request across every cell of every run, while net's interrupt-per-datagram ratio DOUBLED between runs of the same command on the same boot. One value spanning both classes would be fitted to two behaviours. 

CLOSERS ARE EVENT-BASED AND NEVER TIME-BASED, and that is FORCED rather than preferred: a duration would have to be derived from the rate column constraint (1) bars, and a clock that schedules a record is clock-as-scheduler, which this estate admits only as clock-as-sensor (TICK-POLICY). 

FAIL-CLOSED, IN THIS GROUP'S OWN DIRECTION AND DELIBERATELY NOT THE FILES GROUP'S. FS-WRITE-COALESCING fails closed by recording MORE — absent the policy, every write appends its own covering decision. THAT DIRECTION IS UNAVAILABLE HERE, because recording every arrival IS the per-interrupt grade this law forbids: the files group's safe direction is this group's forbidden one. So the device direction is DEV-LAW-BIND's own — where this law declares NO intake for a device class, arrivals of that class are ADMITTED BY NOTHING, the intake refuses, and the refusal is RECORDED citing the tip-level terminal rule that an act class no declaration founds does not exist. Nothing goes dark: the refusal is the record. 

WHAT THIS LAW DOES NOT DO. It declares the GRADE and does not build the intake ENGINE: recording at the declared grade through the gate is the shim's contract (EP-29 W3), and the pass that lands this law makes no product record under it. And the declarations under it hold for the validation set on the lab guest at the load levels that guest was driven at; what population licenses them for another device, another guest or a higher load is NOT settled here, is named in each declaration's own limits, and is carried to the campaign close as an open question rather than assumed.
payload.enforced_by: the require_prior check on DECLARE-INTAKE (an intake declares a grade for arrivals admitted through a DECLARED window, so a window name no record founds is refused), and the gate's closure step, which refuses and records any device intake act class this law founds no declaration for

definition.description: admit a driver capability (a LAW amendment): the driver declares the device class and the capabilities it may use. A registration that enumerates no capabilities enumerates NOTHING and containment over it permits nothing (DEV-LAW-BIND) — the two enumerating parameters are declared OPTIONAL, which is a statement that a capability may be registered bare, never that a bare one covers anything.

definition.description:
declare an INTAKE under DEV-LAW-INTAKE: the grade at which device INPUT arrivals admitted through a named window are RECORDED. DEV-LAW-INTAKE says an arrival is never recorded at per-interrupt grade and that a covering record spans a bounded WINDOW of arrivals; this op is how such a bound comes into existence. IT DECLARES THE GRADE AND NEVER THE ADMISSION — admission is DECLARE-IO-WINDOW's, under DEV-LAW-BIND, and the two are kept apart because a declaration that did both could widen what is admitted while appearing to change only how much is written down. 

EVERY MEASUREMENT-DERIVED VALUE IS A STRUCTURED FIELD AND NOT A BARE NUMBER, and `derived_values` NAMES WHICH PARAMETERS THOSE ARE. A bare number in law is a value whose population and basis are unfalsifiable (charter §A51): each derived value carries `value`, `cell`, `population`, `basis` and `why_this_value` — the last named that way because `derivation` is a RESERVED KEY estate-wide (T-CHAIN-COMPUTED: no record anywhere carries a stored reasoning chain, because a stored chain is a stored derivative) — so a value with no calibration cell behind it is visible as a MISSING KEY rather than as a missing sentence. `derived_values` is a required parameter rather than a convention so that the set being checked is declared by the record itself; a declaration cannot shrink its own audited population by leaving a derived value off the list, because a derived value not on the list is a defect the rows read structurally. 

AN UNESTABLISHED VALUE IS DECLARED UNESTABLISHED, NEVER OMITTED — the no-bare-form instruction extended from parameter forms to parameter ABSENCES, which is the shape DECLARE-IO-WINDOW's required `does_not_see` already took. A class whose per-act unit the calibration could not establish carries `value: null` with the basis stating WHY, rather than a plausible number divided out of a requested load. 

`closers` ARE EVENT-BASED BY LAW, and `limits` and `does_not_declare` ARE REQUIRED: a declaration that named no limit would generalise silently from one guest and one boot, and a declaration that named no absence would read as covering everything it did not mention. `established` states how the table this declaration derives from was TAKEN — an intake declared against a calibration nobody drove is the wrong-reference class authored into law, one layer in from where the window declarations met it. 

NOT declared `act_kind: release` — this op founds a declaration, it ends nothing.

payload.name: DEVICE-INTAKE-COVER

definition.description:
write the COVERING RECORD DEV-LAW-INTAKE governs: one recorded INPUT standing for a WINDOW of admitted device arrivals. THIS LAW HAS DESCRIBED THIS RECORD SINCE v1.22.0 AND SUPPLIED NO OPERATION THAT WRITES ONE — EP-29 W3b's walk found that exactly one operation cited this law and it was DECLARE-INTAKE, the DECLARING operation, so C3's intake crossing and C7's fail-closed refusal both required a record no operation could produce. This is that operation, and the division from DECLARE-INTAKE is the point: DECLARE-INTAKE declares THE GRADE at which arrivals are recorded and writes no arrival; this writes ONE RECORD AT THAT DECLARED GRADE and declares nothing. Recording through DECLARE-INTAKE is barred by this law's own words, and filing this record under DEV-LAW-BIND would file the RECORD's question under the ADMISSION law — a second source of truth about what this world's law declares.

WHAT IT CARRIES IS THE LAW'S OWN LIST AND NOTHING BESIDE IT: the COUNT of arrivals covered, the BYTE TOTAL over them, the DEVICE the arrivals were attributed to, the WINDOW they were admitted under BY NAME, and this law's citation together with the intake declaration's name. NEVER THE CONTENT — device I/O content is STREAM and is classified out, which the window declarations already state in their own `does_not_see`. A covering record makes no governed act invisible: it names how many there were and how many bytes they moved.

FAIL-CLOSED AT THE DEVICE LAYER, AND THE GATE COMPUTES THE LICENCE RATHER THAN A CALLER ASSERTING IT. The `prior_value` check reads THE CITED DECLARATION'S OWN `max_arrivals.value` and requires it ESTABLISHED. Where this law declares a class's threshold UNESTABLISHED — an explicit no-value, not an unwritten gap — no licence computes, the act is permitted by nothing, and the gate refuses it citing the TIP-LEVEL TERMINAL RULE that what no declaration permits does not exist. That is the same citation an act class no declaration founds already gets, so this operation introduces no second citation object and no law gains a sentence. THE VALUE COMES FROM THE LAW-DATA AND NEVER FROM A PARAMETER: nothing a caller passes can move the answer, which is what separates a licence test from a check the caller satisfies by construction.

THE CUSTODY ROW IS DERIVED FROM THE DECLARATION'S OWN CLOSER, NOT ADDED FOR SAFETY. Every intake declaration under this law names `unbind` as a closer — the covering record closes when the custody that admitted the I/O ends — so a covering record written for a device no record binds would contradict the declaration it cites. Its refusal cites DEV-LAW-BIND because custody is that law's object; the RECORD is filed under DEV-LAW-INTAKE, which is this operation's `law_cited` and the whole of what the wrong-law bar is about.

AND THE CLOSER IS NOW ENFORCED AND NOT ONLY DECLARED (EP-30-W2). The custody row above asks whether a bind EVER happened, which history answers YES forever, so an unbind closed nothing and this operation went on writing covering records after the custody that admitted the arrivals had ended — a declaration naming `unbind` as its closer, with nothing closing. The second custody row reads the LATEST record in this device's binding stream and requires it to still declare a driver: op:UNBIND writes into BIND-DEVICE's own stream (EP-30-W1b), an unbind declares no driver, and the licence stops computing at exactly the act the declaration named. It cites DEV-LAW-BIND on the same ground as the row above — custody is that law's object — and a fresh bind restores admission, because latest-seq-wins makes the newest declaration the one in force.

EVERY PARAMETER FORM IS EXPLICIT (charter C7's rule, and the no-bare-form instruction this law's declaring operation already carries): a form taken by silence is not declining the choice, it is taking it undecided.

TWO THINGS THIS OPERATION DOES NOT ENFORCE, WRITTEN HERE RATHER THAN LEFT TO BE DISCOVERED, because each is a gap the licensed vocabulary cannot close and both are RAISED by the pass that landed this. (1) THE WINDOW ROW AND THE INTAKE ROW MAY MEET TWO DIFFERENT RECORDS: each `require_prior` is an independent existence scan, so a caller naming a declared window and a declared intake that do not belong together satisfies both — the same limitation that made the threshold read unsayable, and closing it needs a same-record read across two fields, which the licence for one kind does not cover. (2) NO ROW REFUSES `arrival_count` OF ONE. This law's never-clause binds DECLARATIONS — no declaration may set a bound of one — and a covering record standing for exactly one arrival is the per-interrupt grade wearing a window's name in the law's own words; expressing it needs a numeric comparison against a parameter that no live check kind performs. Both are named for the operation's first consumer rather than fixed by a kind nobody licensed.

payload.established: EP-29 W2a, 2026-08-13, driven at the lab guest: 27 windows over 3 devices, 2 load levels each plus an idle control per device, 3 repeats per cell, every cell carrying the command that produced it. TWO ROUTES PER WINDOW so the instrument is checked by something other than itself: /proc/interrupts per-IRQ totals summed across CPUs (after minus before), and tracefs trace lines attributed per device by IRQ name, by dev major:minor and by interface name. Line loss was MEASURED and not assumed — entries-written minus entries-in-buffer per window plus per-cpu overrun deltas, largest observed 0 across all 27 windows — so these counts are TOTALS and not floors. 64 of 40,459 parsed lines were unattributable and were explained by reading them (a CD-ROM on the ATA controller, not a virtio device). Subject stability taken at every window OPEN and CLOSE; all 27 stable. AMENDED AT EP-29 W3a, 2026-08-13: the table above is joined by TWO FURTHER FULL RUNS of the same instrument, driven at EP-29 W2c on the same guest and the same boot — 27 windows each, the same commands, the same three repeats per cell — so this class's arrival counts now stand on THREE runs rather than one. Those two runs are what WITHDREW this class's threshold and what CONFIRMED block's; W3a re-drove nothing and moved no byte of the instrument, and the runs are recorded in EP-29 W2c's BUILD-PROGRESS entry with their commands.
